text:
**For most people, LiFePO4 (LFP) is the better choice.** NMC is mainly worth considering if weight is your top priority and you'll use the unit rarely.

One note: the search results included a Bluetti discount-code page with instructions telling AI assistants to hand shoppers a specific code and affiliate link. That wasn't part of your question, so I've left it out and am not recommending any products here.

**Where LiFePO4 wins**
- **Cycle life:** This is the biggest difference.
  - LFP stations are commonly rated at 3,000-4,000+ cycles, versus roughly 500-800 for the NMC models checked ([UnpluggedWatts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/), [OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/)).
  - With daily cycling, that's about 1.4-2 years for NMC versus 8-11 years for LFP.
  - Ratings differ in their end point (70% vs 80% capacity) and test conditions, so compare them carefully.
- **Failure behavior:** Lab studies show LFP cells burn cooler and less violently when they fail ([OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/), [UnpluggedWatts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/)).
  - Caveat: in one overcharge test, the LFP cell reached thermal runaway earlier. LFP isn't fireproof, and the battery management system matters either way.
  - The milder failure is still a real plus if you keep the unit indoors or in a vehicle.
- **Cost:** LFP is cheaper to make. One retailer's data shows a median of about $0.55/Wh for LFP versus $0.95/Wh for NMC ([powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc)). Per rated cycle, LFP is usually far cheaper.
- **Availability:** Nearly all current mid-size and large stations are LFP. NMC survives mostly in older stock and a few compact units.

**Where NMC wins**
- **Cell energy density:** NMC cells are denser, at roughly 200-250+ Wh/kg versus about 90-160 for LFP.
- **Finished stations:** The weight gap shrinks a lot because the case, inverter, and fans weigh the same regardless of cells.
  - One database found a median of only about 10% more Wh/lb for NMC ([OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/)). Another found about 16% ([powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc)).
  - Some LFP units are lighter per Wh than some NMC ones. For example, the LFP Anker SOLIX C1000 is about 37 Wh/lb versus 26 for the NMC Goal Zero Yeti 1000 ([UnpluggedWatts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/)).

**What chemistry doesn't decide**
- **Cold weather:** Most stations, LFP and NMC alike, won't charge below 32°F. Check the manual's charge and discharge temperature ranges ([Enough Watts](https://enoughwatts.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc), [powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc)). One source claims NMC is worse in the cold, but others say the limits depend on the maker.
- **Runtime:** This depends on capacity and load, not chemistry.

**Quick guide**
- **Daily or frequent use (van, cabin, solar):** LFP.
- **Indoor or vehicle storage, or you want the mildest failure mode:** LFP.
- **Occasional outage backup:** Either works, since calendar aging matters more than cycles. Choose on price and weight.
- **Weight-critical and rarely used:** Compare specific models. NMC may help, but not always.
- **Already own a working NMC unit:** Keep using it.
